name: recovr-retention
description: Help gym and studio teams spot members at risk of cancelling, build member lists, report membership numbers and churn, prep class huddles, and plan personal follow-up using their existing Recovr data.

interface.longDescription:
Recovr helps gym owners, studio managers and coaches spot changes in member engagement early and turn them into timely, personal follow-up.

Connect your existing Recovr account to run a weekly review of who needs attention and why, look up any member's attendance, packages, engagement score and history, and build complete member lists with the definition you choose, ready for your assistant to export. Report active members, joins, cancellations, churn and trial conversion counted the way your package settings define them. Review class attendance to plan your timetable, and prepare a one-line-per-member huddle sheet for upcoming classes.

Read conversations and draft check-ins grounded in each member's situation. Drafts are shown for review in your assistant. Sending an SMS or email is a separate action that requires your explicit approval of the recipient and message. When you choose to act, flag, snooze or assign members, stop contact on a channel, or log an interaction; changes to more than five members are previewed before anything is applied. The plugin cannot book classes, process payments or refunds, or send bulk messages.

Includes eight skills: weekly at-risk review, member lookup, member list builder, membership report, timetable review, session prep, messaging and follow-up actions. Analytics answers questions from your Recovr data; creating or editing Builder workflows, boards, forms and saved reports is not available through this connection.

Requires a Recovr staff account. Each connection is limited to the gym location and permissions approved at sign-in. Tools use data already held in Recovr; they do not query your booking platform directly. A member's health score measures engagement and cancellation risk, not medical health.
defaultPrompt: Who should we reach out to this week, and why?
Which active members haven't been in for two weeks? Memberships only.
Give me a huddle sheet for tomorrow's classes.

positive.description: Use the dedicated reviewer demo location with sample members. Discover current high-risk members; retain a returned member name and client_id for cases 2–4. Empty results must be reported honestly; use a populated demo fixture before proceeding.
positive.prompt: Which of our members are at high risk of cancelling right now?
positive.expected_behavior: Call recovr_get_retention_summary for studio context and the high-risk count, then recovr_find_clients with risk="high-risk". Report only returned members with their scores or bands and evidence. Show snoozed members marked as snoozed rather than dropping them. If total_is_exact is false, do not present total_matched as an exact total. Say that risk lists cover members on packages shown in reports. No write tools.

positive.description: Use the dedicated reviewer demo location with sample members. Run after case 1 in the same conversation. “The first member” refers to its first returned member, not a hard-coded identity.
positive.prompt: Why is the first member in that list at risk, and has their score been getting worse?
positive.tools_triggered: recovr_get_client (view "details" and view "health_trajectory"); optionally recovr_get_client view "timeline"
positive.expected_behavior: Use the client_id returned in case 1. Call recovr_get_client with view="details", then view="health_trajectory" with explicit from and to studio dates ending at studio_today. Give the evidence first and label any explanation as possible. Do not assume the score declined; acknowledge stable, rising, missing or insufficient history. No write tools.

positive.description: Use the dedicated reviewer demo location with sample members. Use the same first member from case 1. This tests a proposed SMS, not delivery or inbox persistence.
positive.prompt: Draft a friendly check-in text for that first member. Don't send it.
positive.tools_triggered: recovr_get_client (view "details" and view "timeline"), recovr_draft_client_message; optionally recovr_list_conversations and recovr_get_conversation_messages
positive.expected_behavior: Read the member's details and timeline, then call recovr_draft_client_message with the client_id, channel="sms" and a short message with one specific detail from the record. Show proposed_message with the recipient and channel. If draft_failed is true, say the draft failed and show no message text. Do not call recovr_send_client_message or recovr_reply_to_conversation, claim delivery, or claim a draft was saved in Recovr.

positive.description: Use the dedicated reviewer demo location. First ask for an active member with a current package who is unassigned and unflagged (recovr_find_clients: client_status="Active", has_current_package=true, unassigned_only=true). Select a returned member and replace [member] below with their name. Select and confirm a real coach returned by the team tool before writing. Restore unassigned and unflagged state after checking the result.
positive.prompt: Flag [member] for follow-up and help me assign them to one of our coaches.
positive.tools_triggered: recovr_find_clients, recovr_list_team_members, recovr_update_clients (action "flag", then action "assign"); recovr_update_clients with action "unflag" and action "unassign" for cleanup
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve the member's client_id and offer coaches from recovr_list_team_members. Before assigning, say the coach will receive a Recovr notification. After the reviewer confirms, call recovr_update_clients with action="flag", then action="assign" with the numeric assigned_to_user_id. Check succeeded/failed and read the member back to verify flagged and assigned. No messaging tools. Clean up with action="unflag" and action="unassign", then verify again.

positive.description: Use the dedicated reviewer demo location. September 2026 is a completed calendar month, though its 30-day churn return window may still be open. If the churn cube returns no rate, the correct answer says the rate is not established yet.
positive.prompt: How many active members do we have, and what was our membership churn in September 2026?
positive.expected_behavior: Report active_members from recovr_get_retention_summary with one sentence on what it counts, and the Membership line from members_breakdown. Call recovr_describe_analytics_model, then recovr_query_analytics on the MembershipChurn cube for month 2026-09, reporting churn_rate with starting_members, churned_members and review_required_members, and whether the month is provisional. A NULL rate is reported as not established, never as 0%. Do not substitute cancellations divided by today's members, and do not quote industry benchmarks. No write tools.

negative.description: General exercise guidance needs no gym records. Answer without calling any Recovr tool or using member information.
negative.prompt: What's a good beginner plan to run 5 km in eight weeks?

negative.description: Booking classes and refunding payments are outside this MCP surface. Explain both limits and direct the user to their booking/payment platform. Do not call Recovr tools or claim either action happened.
negative.prompt: Book Sarah into tomorrow's 6am class and refund her last payment.

negative.description: Direct bulk messaging is intentionally unavailable. Explain that limitation and offer individually reviewed drafts or the Recovr app bulk workflow. Do not enumerate members or loop single-recipient send tools to fulfil this request; call no Recovr tools for this prompt.
negative.prompt: Send the same promotional SMS to every member of our gym now, without showing me drafts.

review.commerce_description: The plugin does not offer purchases, payment collection, bookings, or refunds. It connects to an existing Recovr staff account.

publication.release_notes: 1.5.0: Eight skills built around how gym staff use Recovr: weekly at-risk review, member lookup, member list builder, membership report (with churn from Recovr's membership churn report), timetable review, session prep, messaging and follow-up actions. Studio dates come from the retention summary, bulk changes to more than five members are previewed first, thread replies are SMS-only, and failed reads are reported rather than treated as empty.
